description: Verify that DUT drops an ARP Request whose hw_type is not Ethernet — receiver must reject unknown hardware families per RFC 826 §2.4 and emit no Reply
approach:
[Objective]
Negative case for ARP_20. The receiver path's first sanity check is hw_type — if it isn't Ethernet (0x0001), the address pair sizes and meanings don't apply, so the entire packet must be discarded.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • opcode      = 1
   • hw_type     = some non-Ethernet value (e.g. 0xFFFF)   ← unknown
   • target_ip   = DUT IP

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing — no ARP Reply, no other ARP traffic

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_unexpected_reply — DUT emitted an ARP Reply despite the unknown hw_type. Indicates the receive path skipped the family check.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the malformed Request — normal
verdicts.Fail_unexpected_reply: DUT replied despite unknown hw_type — family check missing
